solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Analyse Eastern adherent of monotheistc sect

parts.note: to analyse a sentence grammatically is to parse it

explanation.surface: A request to study a follower of a single-god religion from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' reads as part of the description, but it only supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsees are Zoroastrians of Indian descent, followers of a religion worshipping one god.

clue.text: Competent English Queen participating in an engagement

indicators.note: participating in says the first pieces go inside the engagement

parts.note: a date is an engagement or appointment

explanation.surface: A capable English queen takes part in an appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means satisfactory or competent enough for the purpose.

clue.text: It can help one entering court

definitions.text: It can help one entering court

parts.words: It can help one entering court
parts.note: seems to describe aid for someone going into a law court, but a court is a type of shoe, and this tool eases a foot in

explanation.walkthrough: A court shoe is a plain women's shoe; the tool helps a foot 'enter' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoehorn is a curved implement that eases your heel into a shoe.

clue.text: Eat morsel that's horrible rubbery stuff

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that eating a nasty bit of food is like chewing rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges EATMORSEL; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastomer is a polymer with elastic properties, such as rubber.

clue.text: No cure — it is awful suffering mentally

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gloomy verdict that an ailment cannot be treated and is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges NOCURE and IT; 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic person is one troubled by anxiety or other mental distress.

clue.text: Novel by a Bronte surprisingly full of hot wrath

indicators.note: full of says the rearranged letters hold the next pieces
surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
anger is wrath or rage

explanation.surface: A Bronte novel unexpectedly brimming with hot fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns BYABRONTE into NORT ... ABBEY, which is 'full of' H and ANGER. It is by Jane Austen, not a Bronte.
explanation.definitionFit: Northanger Abbey is Jane Austen's novel satirising Gothic fiction.

clue.text: Come back into section of green territory

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Return to part of a grassy area.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to go back into a place you left.

clue.text: Mark has got together with Heather — that's exciting!

parts.note: a tick is a mark on paper showing something is right
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Mark has started dating Heather, and what a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant ling; 'has got together with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickling can mean pleasantly stimulating or amusing, so exciting.

clue.text: A board member, he's entertained by Civil Service staff

indicators.note: entertained by says the word is held inside the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
to man is to staff, providing workers

explanation.surface: A company director is hosted by civil servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A board member' suggests a director; it is a piece on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman is a piece used on the chessboard.

clue.text: Hungarian obedient? To some extent the reverse — carefree

indicators.note: the reverse tells us the run of letters found is to be read backwards
only part of the words is used, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Hungarian is obedient, then suggests he is partly the opposite, a free spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' picks out RIANOBED from hungaRIAN OBEDient, and 'the reverse' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and light-hearted, untroubled by cares.

clue.text: Engineers given second signal will be free from danger

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a cue is a signal to act or speak

explanation.surface: Engineers receive a second signal before setting people loose from peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them, freeing them from harm or peril.

clue.text: Bird has fun heading off back with straw for home?

indicators.note: back says the shortened word is read in reverse
heading off means the first letter of the word is cut away

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
thatch is straw used to roof a house

explanation.surface: A bird enjoys itself, then heads back with straw to build a nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' leaves UN from FUN, and 'back' turns it into NU.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small European bird that climbs tree trunks head-first.

clue.text: In centre of Brussels there will be long delays

indicators.note: In says one piece goes within the other
centre of picks the middle letters of the word that follows

parts.note: tall and long both describe great length

explanation.surface: A complaint about long hold-ups in the middle of the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link to the city, but it is the container signal; 'there will be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalls are hold-ups or stoppages, as when an engine or process stalls.

clue.text: Message that something still needs to be done about bodyguard

definitions.text: Message that something still needs to be done

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a minder is a person employed to protect someone

explanation.surface: A note about a bodyguard who has a job still to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a prompt telling you a task remains outstanding.

clue.text: Small plant you found hidden in the middle of Hebe, correct?

indicators.note: found hidden in says one piece is tucked inside the other
the middle of picks the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: ye is an old word for you
right means correct

explanation.surface: Asks whether a little plant was tucked away among the shrub hebe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' takes EB from HEBE, with YE 'found hidden in' it, then RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used to treat eye ailments.

clue.text: Plant in wet ground that spreads across river

indicators.note: the wet ground stretches over the river, so it surrounds it

parts.note: a fen is low, marshy land

explanation.surface: A plant grows in boggy land stretching across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless green plant with feathery fronds.

clue.text: Female became different and stumbled

parts.note: altered means changed, became different

explanation.surface: A woman changed and then tripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Faltered means stumbled or hesitated.

clue.text: One tries to be logical about a boy with hesitation

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a boy
er is a hesitant noise in speech

explanation.surface: Someone attempts logic regarding a lad who hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoner is a person who thinks things through logically.

clue.text: Opposing Victorian child-exploiter: 'Off with his head!'

indicators.note: the cry calls for the top of the character to be removed, his first letter

parts.note: Fagin, in Dickens's Oliver Twist, runs a gang of child pickpockets

explanation.surface: A cry against a Victorian villain who exploited children, demanding his execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off with his head' is the Queen of Hearts' cry, used here to chop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect word meaning against, so it means opposed to something.

clue.text: Regarding province, say nothing to shock

parts.note: as to means regarding or concerning
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
sh is a call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about a province in order to shock.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is often called 'the Province' in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze or surprise greatly.

clue.text: Secret American manoeuvres

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving things about, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Covert US military exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera means in private, out of public view, as in closed court sessions.

clue.text: Indian lords, heartless folk making slow progress

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: peers are members of the nobility, lords

explanation.surface: Indian noblemen described as cruel people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks to India, but means the Cree of North America; 'heartless' drops the middle E of PEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepers are people who crawl or move stealthily and slowly.

clue.text: Children's game — defeats being reported

indicators.note: being reported means the word is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: conquers means defeats

explanation.surface: A children's game where losses are recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: CONKERS is a British game where children swing horse chestnuts on strings to smash an opponent's.
explanation.definitionFit: Conkers is a playground game played with horse chestnuts on strings.

clue.text: What is't that completes fine infusion?!

definitions.meaning: a riddle about the word fine, whose final letter finishes it; the reply, in old style, is that it is an E
an infusion is a drink made by steeping herbs in hot water

explanation.walkthrough: Answer the riddle in archaic style: ''Tis an E', since E is the letter ending 'fine'. Run together, those words make the herbal drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tisane is a herbal tea, a drink made by steeping leaves or flowers.

clue.text: She may need to come down to earth

definitions.text: She may need to come down to earth

parts.words: She may need to come down to earth
parts.note: reads like a woman with her head in the clouds needing realism, but literally means a female flier who must land

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down to earth' sounds like advice to a dreamer; here it means landing an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airwoman is a female aviator or member of an air force, who flies and lands.

clue.text: River racer?

definitions.meaning: a river is something that runs, flowing water
a racer is an athlete competing on foot

explanation.walkthrough: A river runs, so cryptically it is a thing that runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that runs, whether flowing water or a sprinter, can be called this.

clue.text: Dire end to time in hospital unit covered in muck

indicators.note: in says the first pieces sit inside the hospital unit

parts.note: a bed is the unit by which hospital capacity is counted
grim means dire or dreadful

indicators.note: end to picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A grim end comes to someone's time on a hospital ward, all filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end to' takes E from TIME; GRIM and E go 'in' BED.
explanation.definitionFit: Begrimed means made dirty with ingrained soot or grime.

clue.text: Is nothing in Ulster city ridiculous?

indicators.note: in says the first pieces are placed within the city

parts.note: Derry, also called Londonderry, is a city in Northern Ireland
taken as written
O, shaped like zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Asks whether nothing in a Northern Irish city is laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or poor as to be laughable.

clue.text: The drunk stood for election in the capital

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
to run for office is to stand for election, and ran is its past

explanation.surface: A drunk stood as a candidate in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles THE into TEH; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.
